item.title: Bible Studies for Life Sunday School Lesson for March 15
item.description: Here’s the Bible Studies for Life Sunday School Lesson for March 15, written by Rony Kozman, Ph.D., Assistant professor of Biblical Studies, Samford University.

item.title: First person: New missionaries share what surprised them the most
item.description: Sometimes it takes two hours just to get groceries. A doctor’s visit will most likely require Google Translate at some point. Air pollution skyrockets during winter months. Language learning is not for the faint of heart.

item.title: First person: Questions for encouraging effective fruitfulness
item.description: People want to succeed. It is inbred in each one of us. Have you ever known anyone to get out of bed in the morning stating, “Today, I want to fail.”? People want to succeed.

item.title: McIntosh named chair of WMU search committee seeking candidates for executive director
item.description: Candace McIntosh, executive director of Alabama WMU, has been named chair of the search committee to seek the National WMU’s next executive director-treasurer.

item.title: Gov. Ivey: Deadline to apply for internship program March 13
item.description: Governor Kay Ivey on Monday reminded college students across Alabama that Friday, March 13, 2026, is the deadline to apply for the Governor’s Office Summer Internship Program.

item.title: Senate bill would increase penalties for fentanyl
item.description: A bill pending in the Alabama Senate would put the penalties for possession of a mixture of synthetic fentanyl and the controlled substances used to make it on par with possession of the deadly drug alone.

item.title: Pleasant View hosts Pylant Family
item.description: Pleasant View Missionary Baptist Church, Holly Pond, will host a singing March 15 at 5 p.m. featuring The Pylant Family. For more information, call 256-339-1862 or 256-590-1501. Earl Harper is pastor.

item.title: What’s zero calories, yet very satisfying? Hint: It’s not your breakfast cereal.
item.description: "Okay, now they’ve gone too far. Now they’re telling me that breakfast cereal is terrible for you."

item.title: Seeking the truth: Christian’s death sparks protest, calls for police action
item.description: A Christian farmworker appears to have been tortured to death by his employers, who then staged the scene to look like suicide.

item.title: Longtime campus minister Frank McCollough dies
item.description: Frank McCollough served as the Baptist Campus Minister at the University of Miami, then for a combined 18 years at Auburn University and the University of Montevallo. He retired in 1996.
